title: Continuous integration applied to the network

videos.script: Lesson 13's checks work when somebody remembers to run them. On a Friday afternoon, somebody will not. {{friday}} Continuous integration means nobody has to remember. Every change pushed to the shared repository is tested, automatically. {{ci}} A change that fails is refused before anyone builds on it. {{refuse}} In this lesson the pipeline is two Git hooks on a server. One runs before a push is accepted, and can say no. {{pre}} The other runs after, and deploys what reached main, then checks the network. {{post}} You push lesson 13's bad change, and the server refuses it in a tenth of a second. {{refused}} You push a good one on a branch, merge it, and watch it reach exactly one router. {{merged}} And then you see the same pipeline written for a hosted CI service, with the scripts unchanged. {{service}}
